newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs drift lower, focus on U.S.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs drift lower, focus on U.S.

text.p: BRUSSELS, Jan 30 - Belgian OLOs drifted lower in quiet trading on Thursday as players sat back and focused their attention on the United States where the Federal Reserve chairman was speaking and ahead of GDP data there on Friday.
"We're seeing range-trading and consolidation. People are now waiting for GDP," one dealer said, adding that a domestic political scandal was having little actual impact on prices.

U.S. Treasuries provided support, remaining well bid after unsurprising weekly jobless claims and after the Federal Reserve's Alan Greenspan said the consumer price index was overstating inflation by 0.5 to 1.5 percentage points a year.
By 1540 GMT the benchmark 10-year OLO was yielding 5.85 percent compared to a previous close of 5.87, its yield premium over equivalent Bunds widened one basis point to six bp.

"Six has been the average for a month," one dealer noted, adding that he did not attribute Thursday's slight spread widening to an errupting bribery scandal in the Francophone PS socialist party, one of the four parties in Belgium's centre-left coalition government.
On Thursday pressure on the government increased as a liberal opposition party offered to swap places in the coalition with the PS.
However the Flemish Christian Democrat party - the largest coalition party - dismissed the idea saying it was not at the stage of changing partners.
"Everyone is talking a lot - (but) we're not yet at the stage of a political crisis," the dealer added.
